transcript.text: Thanks for joining. Today we are aligning on the ThinkBionics pilot: a searchable meeting workspace, reliable summaries, and clear next steps.
Our customer success team loses context between discovery and implementation. We need every promise to have an owner and a link back to the conversation.
The key requirement is traceability. Every action item and note should link to the exact moment in the recording, so nobody has to rewatch the entire call.
We can support timestamped transcripts and a Jira issue draft in the first pilot. A real Jira connection will require a separate permissions review.
For the interface, keep the recording on the left and action items on the right. Transcript, summary, and Ask Fathom should stay one click away.
Can the team search by speaker and ask who owns the follow-up? That is especially useful after an hour-long call with eight people.
Agreed. We will ship transcript search, speaker filters, and source-linked answers in the pilot. The beta review is Monday, October 12.
I will prepare the transcript import and review the Jira permissions checklist by Friday, October 9. The tracking issue is FAT-142.
I will finish the split-view prototype and check its mobile layout by Friday. I will also document how notes jump back into playback.

I will invite the customer success pilot group on Monday and gather feedback on summary quality. Let us keep sharing private until the access review is finished. The customer success team should prepare a rollout checklist after launch.
One risk remains: Jira permissions may take longer than the UI work. We can validate local issue drafts without sending anything to Jira. Someone should review the AI summary by Friday.
Perfect. Our decisions are clear: a Monday beta review, traceable notes, and a private pilot. Thanks everyone; the summary and owners will be ready for follow-up.
